note: Reviewed by the owner on 2026-10-19 (docs/I18N_PLAN.md §4). The list picked when answering “Which direction feels most needed right now?” at the end of a session. It is a direction the user tries on for now; the app never says “this is what you really need.”

fieldNotes.responses: Things that can actually be tried in that direction after closing the app. Limited to two to four, with an option not to do anything at the end.
fieldNotes.because: Why these options are showing. The only basis is the need the user picked. No claims about psychological mechanisms and no prescriptive wording.
fieldNotes.route: A need that leads to more exploring inside the app rather than to an action outside it.
fieldNotes.exit: An option to finish without a response.
fieldNotes.group: Labels that group the list so it is easy to scan. They do not mean one direction is better, and the order is not a recommendation. The pleasant directions are mixed in so they are not pushed to the bottom of the list.

needs.label: Adjusting the pace of body and mind a little
needs.because: Because you chose “Adjusting the pace of body and mind,” here are a few small things to try with your body right now.

responses.label: Notice your body for a moment, without forcing your breathing or posture to change
Gently move one spot that feels tense
Change your seat or position a little, then notice again
Leave it here for now

needs.label: Staying a little longer with a good moment
needs.because: Because you chose “Staying with a good moment,” here are a few ways to take it in a little more and keep something of it.

responses.label: Pause and notice what feels good in your body now
Write one sentence about what was good
Share it with someone
Keep a scene or feeling you want to remember

needs.label: Sorting out thoughts
needs.because: Because you chose “Sorting out thoughts,” here are ways to move what is in your head onto paper.

responses.label: Write down the facts and your reading of them separately
Write down only the one thing on your mind most
Separate what can be decided now from what cannot
Set it aside to look at again later

needs.label: Looking at what helped this good moment come about
needs.because: Because you chose “Looking at what helped,” here are ways to look back at what came along with this experience.

responses.label: Look back at what the situation was
Notice who you were with, or whether you were alone
Write down what in the place or activity helped
Think about whether these conditions could come together again

needs.label: Understanding this experience a little more
needs.because: Because you chose “Understanding a little more,” this leads to a place in the app for looking a little further.

needs.label: Getting ready to tell someone
needs.because: Because you chose “Getting ready to tell someone,” here are ways to sort out what to say before saying it.

First consider whether now is the time to talk

responses.label: Write down one person who comes to mind
Write in one sentence what you would ask for

Not right now

needs.because: Because you chose “Deciding on a step,” here are ways to start without making it big.

Leave the next step for later
